content.comment_body: Hello everyone. I attempted to download my program to my [product_name] device, and it's prompting for a password. I haven’t set any password since I just created the project, and the device is brand new. Any advice?
That's quite unusual. Could you share a screenshot to clarify exactly where the password prompt appears? Try using "logo" or "LOGO" as the password.
Here is what I see: After I select transfer > PC to [product_name], the connection is successful but then this password prompt pops up.
Give this a try: Go to Tools > Transfer > delete user program and password.
I've already tried that, but the same password prompt appears. It doesn't make sense.
Turns out the password was LOGO. I tried "logo" and "" before. Frustrating!
Glad to hear it's resolved. Thanks for the update.

Hello all! I have a similar issue—when I try to switch to admin via the [product_name] itself, it asks for a password. I’ve tried "LOGO", "logo", "", "admin", "Admin" and other variations, but none work. Any suggestions?
When you receive a new [product_name], the default password to switch to Admin Mode is "LOGO". If that's not accepted, it means the password has been changed.
So if I delete the program and password using [product_name] configuration software, should the password reset?
Thank you; the correct password was LOGO. Surprising that [company_name] doesn't provide documentation or instructions with new devices regarding the default password. Thanks again.
You can download the user manual for [product_name] from [company_name], which details menu access protection and passwords in Chapter 3.5.
A new question by [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread about disabling password protection for downloads or online access. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users report confusion and frustration when their newly set up or reset [product_name] devices unexpectedly request a password during transfers or admin mode changes. There’s a general expectation that either no password or a known factory default should be required, but these prompts sometimes appear anyway. Actions such as attempting to reset or erase the password using software do not consistently resolve the situation, causing uncertainty about the correct procedures.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that new or recently reset devices will either not request a password, or will reliably accept a documented factory default password. If a password reset is performed, users anticipate the device returning to a no-password state or a clearly documented default.
